sections.title: Cooking methods
sections.content:
Precise vocabulary for how food is prepared:
• sauté — fry quickly in a little hot oil. Sauté the onions until golden brown.
• simmer — cook gently just below boiling. Let the sauce simmer for twenty minutes.
• marinate — soak in flavoured liquid before cooking. Marinate the chicken overnight for the best flavour.
• garnish — decorate a dish before serving. Garnish with fresh herbs and serve immediately.
• drizzle — pour a thin stream of liquid. Drizzle olive oil over the salad.

sections.title: Taste and texture
sections.content:
Describing food beyond basic adjectives:
• succulent — tender, juicy, and delicious. The steak was incredibly succulent.
• bland — lacking strong flavour. The soup tasted rather bland without enough seasoning.
• savoury — salty or spicy rather than sweet. I prefer savoury snacks to sweet ones.
• aromatic — having a pleasant, distinctive smell. Aromatic spices filled the kitchen with wonderful scents.
• exquisite — extremely beautiful and delicate. The chef prepared an exquisite five-course meal.

exercises.question: To cook food gently just below boiling point is to:
exercises.explanation: To simmer means to cook just below boiling point with gentle bubbling.

exercises.question: Food that lacks flavour is described as:
exercises.explanation: Bland means lacking strong flavour; mild and uninteresting.

exercises.question: To soak food in a flavoured liquid before cooking is to:
exercises.explanation: To marinate means to soak food in a seasoned liquid before cooking.

exercises.question: A dish that is tender, juicy, and delicious is:
To pour a thin stream of oil or sauce over food is to:
exercises.explanation: To drizzle means to pour a thin stream of liquid over something.

exercises.question: Food that is salty or spicy rather than sweet is:
exercises.explanation: Savoury means belonging to the category of food that is salty or spicy.

exercises.question: To decorate a finished dish before serving is to:
exercises.explanation: To garnish means to decorate food for presentation.

exercises.question: Having a pleasant, distinctive smell is:
exercises.explanation: Aromatic means having a pleasant and distinctive smell.
